correctness.rationale: An independent enumeration considers all permutations from the even color class to the odd class of the cube and retains exactly the 272 supported bijections. Orbit closure under four translations and three adjacent coordinate swaps produces the full cube action and regenerates the eight lexicographic representatives and sizes. For each retained graph, independent subsets are generated via a least-bit recurrence, and an independent subset is maximal exactly when every one-vertex enlargement is disallowed. A support is shattered precisely when the successive positive/negative splits of the bitset of concepts leave every branch nonempty; this is equivalent to the trace equality in the Finding, with no restriction to maximum sets. Testing one-vertex supersets finds all facets by downward closure. All rows of the independent census agree with orbit_data.json, including the distinct maximal-independent-set size distributions, the common initial face counts, 40 VC-dimension-five deletions and 16 pure deletions. A separate backtracking isomorphism test finds a full edge-preserving bijection from GP(8,3) to class 8. The classification is eight orbit-indexed profiles, not eight distinct coefficient pairs: rows 1 and 6 coincide in both face and facet counts. The Finding's table is correct; the title can be read more clearly as a classification across eight orbits.
residual_risks: Only the deletion of an entire perfect matching of Q4 is covered. Cube orbits are not by definition graph isomorphism classes after deletion; here the computed size distributions separate them.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The old graph and edge-insertion graph do not dominate the result: shattering here is defined through maximality in a specific retaining graph, so comparing arbitrary edge changes is not a monotonicity argument for this concept class.

value.rationale: One-factor deletion gives a natural degree-preserving family relative to the deleted edge set: all retained graphs are cubic on the same vertex set and are generated by the same symmetric rule. A complete orbit-indexed census quantifies how this constrained perturbation changes the trace complex rather than simply tabulating isolated graphs. The exact coexistence of different dimensions and purity outcomes, and the identical face/facet vectors for two graphs separable by their concept-size counts, furnish precise comparison data for MIS-shattering and extremal examples such as Möbius–Kantor.
residual_risks: No higher-dimensional stability theorem or general relation between orbit invariants and shattering is proved.
